title: Mao's China: emergence, consolidation and rule
summary: How the Chinese Communist Party won the civil war, how Mao consolidated power after 1949, and the impact of the Great Leap Forward and the Cultural Revolution.

keyterms.definition: 1934–35 retreat of Communist forces from Jiangxi to Yan'an; it later became a founding myth and made Mao leader.
CCP base in north-west China (1935–47) where Mao built his authority, land reform and a cult of leadership.
Chinese Nationalist Party led by Chiang Kai-shek, defeated by the CCP in the civil war and retreated to Taiwan in 1949.
1951–52 campaigns against corruption, waste and bureaucracy in the party, then against capitalists, used to assert control.
1956–57 invitation to criticise the party, followed by the Anti-Rightist Campaign that persecuted critics.
1958–62 campaign for rapid industrial and agricultural growth through people's communes; it caused a catastrophic famine.
Huge collective units created in 1958 merging villages for farming, industry and communal living.
Movement launched by Mao in 1966 to purge 'capitalist roaders' and reassert his authority, using Red Guards; it lasted until 1976.
Student militants who attacked teachers, officials and the 'Four Olds' during the Cultural Revolution.
'Quotations from Chairman Mao', compiled under Lin Biao for the army (1964) and central to the Mao cult.

questions.prompt: Why was the Long March important for Mao?
options: He emerged as the dominant CCP leader after the Zunyi Conference (1935)
It ended in the capture of Beijing
It destroyed the GMD army
It was supported by the USA
questions.explanation: Most marchers died or deserted, but the march gave the party a heroic myth and Mao a leading role.

questions.statement: The CCP strengthened its position during the war against Japan (1937–45) while the GMD was weakened.
questions.explanation: The GMD bore the brunt of conventional fighting, suffered inflation and corruption, while the CCP expanded guerrilla base areas.

questions.text: Mao proclaimed the People's Republic of China on 1 October ___.
questions.explanation: Chiang Kai-shek's government retreated to Taiwan.

questions.prompt: Match each reason to its role in the CCP's civil war victory.
questions.explanation: Historians weigh CCP strengths against GMD weaknesses.

questions.prompt: How did the Korean War (1950–53) help Mao consolidate power?
options: It justified campaigns against 'counter-revolutionaries' and mobilised nationalism
It led to China's occupation of Japan
It forced Mao to share power with the GMD
It ended Soviet aid
questions.explanation: The war created a climate of emergency that the regime used to crush opposition at home.

questions.statement: The Five-Antis campaign targeted capitalists and private businesses.
questions.explanation: It attacked bribery, tax evasion and fraud by businessmen, weakening the private sector.

questions.prompt: Put these events in chronological order.
items: Second United Front with the GMD

questions.text: The 1957 ___ Campaign persecuted those who criticised the party during the Hundred Flowers.
questions.explanation: Hundreds of thousands were labelled rightists, many sent to labour camps.

questions.prompt: What is a key historiographical debate about the Hundred Flowers?
options: Whether Mao genuinely sought criticism or set a trap to expose opponents
Whether it happened at all
Whether it was a Soviet idea
Whether it ended the civil war
questions.explanation: Some see a miscalculation followed by a crackdown; Jung Chang and Jon Halliday argue it was a deliberate trap.

questions.prompt: What did the Agrarian Reform Law of 1950 do?
options: Redistributed landlords' land to peasants, often through violent struggle sessions
Created people's communes
Returned land to the GMD
Ended all farming in the north
questions.explanation: Land reform won peasant support but cost the lives of large numbers of landlords.

lessons.title: Great Leap Forward and Cultural Revolution

questions.prompt: What was the main cause of the famine during the Great Leap Forward?
options: Unrealistic targets, exaggerated reports and grain requisitions combined with misguided farming methods
A US naval blockade
Japanese occupation
Over-production of grain
questions.explanation: Officials reported false harvests, the state took grain based on them, and labour was diverted to backyard furnaces.

questions.text: In 1958 villages were merged into huge people's ___.
questions.explanation: Communes had communal kitchens and organised labour on a military model.

questions.statement: At the 1959 Lushan Conference, Marshal Peng Dehuai's criticism of the Great Leap led to his dismissal.
questions.explanation: Peng's purge silenced critics, so the disastrous policies continued for two more years.

questions.prompt: Which historian estimated at least 45 million premature deaths in the Great Leap famine?
options: Frank Dikötter
John King Fairbank
Robert Conquest
Eric Hobsbawm
questions.explanation: Dikötter's 'Mao's Great Famine' (2010) used provincial archives; other estimates range from about 15 to 45 million.

questions.prompt: Match each person to their role.

pairs.right: Head of state purged as a 'capitalist roader'
Defence minister who promoted the Little Red Book
Mao's wife, member of the Gang of Four
Pragmatist purged twice, later paramount leader

questions.explanation: The Cultural Revolution was partly Mao's struggle to remove pragmatists who had sidelined him after the Leap.

questions.prompt: Put these events in chronological order.
items: Lin Biao dies in a plane crash

questions.prompt: What were the 'Four Olds' that Red Guards attacked?
options: Old customs, culture, habits and ideas
Old soldiers, peasants, workers and students
The four old provinces
Soviet advisers
questions.explanation: Temples, books and artefacts were destroyed, and teachers and officials were humiliated and beaten.

questions.text: From 1968 millions of urban youths were sent to the ___ to learn from peasants.
questions.explanation: The 'Up to the Mountains and Down to the Villages' movement also removed unruly Red Guards from the cities.

questions.statement: Mao used the army to restore order after Red Guard factions fought each other in 1967–68.
questions.explanation: The PLA's role grew greatly, boosting Lin Biao until his fall in 1971.

questions.prompt: Which achievement is often credited to Mao's China despite its human costs?
options: Improved literacy and life expectancy compared with 1949
Full democracy
Higher growth than any other country in the 1960s
An end to all famine by 1960
questions.explanation: Balanced essays weigh gains in health, literacy and women's legal rights (1950 Marriage Law) against famine and repression.
